title: The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick free-energy limiting law
main_claim: For every fixed beta>1, the zero-field SK log partition function F_n(beta), centered and divided by its exact standard deviation, converges in distribution through all n to a nondegenerate, moment-determinate law nu_beta. Also, Var F_n / n^{1/3} converges to a_2(beta) in (0,infinity), with power-rate convergence of all moments of Y_n = n^{-1/6}(F_n^c - E F_n^c).

issues.location: Sections 5-8 (05-inverse.tex, 06-global.tex, 07-budgets.tex, 08-statistics.tex) and the PE imports in Appendix 11
issues.description: This is a coverage caveat, not a gap. Proposition 4.1 (stopped pressure increments, saving x^{5+c}) carries the whole result. It rests on about 5000 lines of pair-inverse, global-accuracy, budget and statistics estimates, plus many results imported from the companion PE, some through modified versions ('reuses the proof of PE Prop 4.1', 'common prelimit temperature' appendix). I did not verify these line by line. The paper's correctness depends on them and on PE Theorem 1.1, the n^{1/6+o(1)} exponent, which is used both to start the stop and to rule out v=0.
issues.evidence: Section 10: 'This proves Proposition~\ref{prop:increment}...'; Appendix 11 lists PE Lemmas 2.1-2.14, 3.3-3.12, 4.1-4.10, 5.3-5.9, 6.1-6.6, 7.6-7.7 as inputs, some in modified form.

coverage:
Read in full: introduction, Section 4 (reduction), Section 9 scalar-compression proof (E5-E9 and the j=2,3,4 cases), Section 10 (parameter order), Appendix 11 (companion interface) and the consequences section. Checked by hand:
(1) Augmentation lemma. The telescoped density has nonnegative coefficients on the convex continuations (v1>=x >= rate x/2). Gauge symmetry shows that pinning a spin leaves the law of G unchanged. The epigraph/Prekopa log-concavity argument holds, the centered exponential CGF is -log(1-2s/x)-2s/x = O(x^{2eps}), and the bound s*d_G <~ x^{eps/2} follows.
(2) Dyadic comparison. The mollifier/stencil remainder is D^{-r-1}, giving error x^{eps-11+(r+1)/2}. The theta-derivative decomposition matches (I). The initial stop value is s^2 Var = x^{2eps-o(1)} = o(x^eps). The endpoint scaling x/ell = N'^{-1/6} holds.
(3) Cumulant interpolation. The error is x^{c'-(k-1)eps} + x^{eps-o(1)}, so the requirement k*eps < c'/2 is sufficient. Positivity v>0 follows from the PE lower bound. The variance of the augmented Y_n is v_n+4.
(4) Identification. B_k(z) = z*sum m_k(l) l^{-1-z}, and z*zeta(1+z) is entire, so the function is holomorphic on Re z > -a. Its Taylor radius about z=1 is therefore >1, which gives absolute convergence and B(0)=a_k. The W_k randomized estimator bounds (4^h, 256^h) check.
(5) Section 9. I verified the scaling table under E6 (k0 ~ ell^-3, chi ~ ell, g ~ ell^3, b0 = chi^-2) for all five monomials at j=2,3,4 against ell^{-(6-j)}. I also derived the consistency of E6 with the scalar PDE rescaling, verified the Ito drift (c-u)t'G_zz^2 and diffusion in E8, the leading terms chi^3 k0 c^2 and g^2 k0^2 v^2/2, the s_k expansions in E7, and the cancellation b0*chi^2 = 1.
(6) Section 10 margin inequalities.
(7) Both corollaries: Chatterjee's OU identity with the gradient inner product (nR^2-1)/2, and the replacement derivatives 1/n and beta*n^{-3/2}.
Sections 2-3 and 5-8 were only skimmed via their statements.
